Every consumer (render, routing, interaction, editor trim) derives its behavior from that declaration. There is no freeform vector path, no per-instance transform, and no plugin-registered shape class, and every mutation flows through the single reducer documented in

Where each piece lives in source (and the recipe for adding a shape) is the implementation tier's to govern.

props.title: Toolbar control sets are deliberately simplified, with no text-formatting tier

text.insert: Object text has no per-object formatting. Bold, strikethrough, link, font, size, and alignment controls are intentionally absent, the workspace theme sets every object's typeface, weight, and sizes, and sticky bodies render live simple markdown instead (D18). props.title: Reference recordings are the visual parity authority

text.insert: Where those def-owned constants come from is itself settled:
(the FigJam and AFFiNE reference screen recordings plus the pixel-sampled

corpus distilled from them) is the single parity authority for every FigJam-derived constant in the engine: colors, radii, stroke widths, spacing, motion. A parity question is settled against the recordings, not any individual engineer's judgment call. Two qualifiers. First, not every value in the analysis corpus is a direct measurement: some are flagged extrapolations for states the recordings never captured (the multi-object selection-toolbar variant is the standing example). Treat an extrapolated constant as a best guess and reconfirm against live FigJam before relying on it for a pixel-exact decision. Second, supersession is explicit, never silent: when shipping geometry deliberately departs from a measured value, the departure is a named decision and the measurement remains documented history. The recording measurement stays the recorded reference even when overruled.

The invariant that fixed editing (D14): RENDERER AND EDITOR CONSUME THE SAME SLOT DESCRIPTOR.
is the one rect/typography source. The at-rest renderer (

In the shipped defs, most shapes take the "center" default (15px, centered, in the theme's name color and weight, which figjam sets to 700 black as D6's baseline). The icon glyph family takes "below" and sticky takes "inset-body". Section takes "title-chip", whose chip counter-scales sub-linearly when zoomed out (titleChipScale() = (1/zoom)^0.6 capped at 6×, geometry in TITLE_CHIP) and sits floating or pinned as the theme places it. Arrow-shape declares a rectTextSlot function (text centers in the body excluding the head). No shipped def declares text: "none" today, but the capability remains: no slot, and textEditing.editable is false, so they refuse the editor.
A slot paints the detail line only when
holds non-blank text, with every whitespace run, newlines included, collapsed to one space. The line sets in the theme's detail typography (
), 3px under the name block, and ellipsizes at the slot width instead of wrapping. Each placement fits it differently:

The name and the detail form one vertically centered block. The detail reserves its line first, so the name loses lines before the detail does, and a slot too short for one name line plus the detail line drops the detail.
An icon's detail follows its label lines, and the band and the painted bounds grow by the gap plus one detail line.
A section's detail renders inline in its header chip after the title, never in a text slot, and a sticky never paints one.
The resolved slot carries the line as

, so the at-rest renderer, the static renderer, and the in-place editor draw the same line. The in-place editor edits the name only and shows the detail beneath its textarea exactly as at rest. props.title: One name plus one fact: the detail line is not a second body

text.insert: The detail line keeps D11's single-text model intact.
stays the one name every kind edits in place, and

holds at most one short fact under it, such as a port, path, version, model, or host. The line is muted, single, and ellipsized rather than wrapped, so prose has nowhere to grow, and explanations go on a sticky beside the subject. Stickies never carry a detail because their markdown body is already the whole note.

props.title: Clicks respect the declared outline. Drag-select and snapping deliberately stay bbox

text.insert: so true-outline shapes are only clickable where they actually paint, while drag-select and snap-candidate gathering remain bounding-box tests on purpose. They are area/alignment semantics, not point-precision semantics, and FigJam behaves the same way. Bbox-outline kinds are byte-identical to the pre-D16 behavior by construction (their outline IS the bbox and no polygon is ever materialized), which is what made the cutover safe to gate on the existing interaction test suite.

props.title: Shape vocabulary is closed and typed, not freeform SVG

text.insert: Extending the shape vocabulary means adding a value to

and registering a def through the closed compile-time vocabularies, not authoring an arbitrary SVG path, a runtime-registered shape class, or a plugin. There is no registration API, no user-supplied path string field, and no mechanism for a canvas document to define a shape the engine doesn't already know how to validate and render. An agent (or a human) constructing a shape only ever writes valid JSON against the schema. The def registry is compile-time, closed, and fully enumerated in
